title: ALMA probes the molecular gas reservoirs in the changing-look Seyfert galaxy Mrk 590
question: Is the AGN in Mrk 590 turning off because of a lack of central molecular gas to fuel it?

data.angular_resolution: CO cube beam 0.47'' x 0.42'' (P.A. -76 deg); Briggs continuum beam 0.34'' x 0.24''
data.sensitivity: CO 1sigma ~0.5 mJy/beam per 20 km/s channel; continuum rms 0.031-0.109 mJy/beam depending on weighting

what.value: Near-IR to far-IR and radio flux densities used for SED fit (UKIRT, VLT, ISO, IRAS, OVRO, VLA, MERLIN)

evidence.quote: We include in our analysis published measurements (summarised in Table [\[continuumfluxpub\]]) of the near-IR to far-IR flux densities of Mrk 590

external_data.citation: (cite: wardetal87; horstetal09; garciaespinosa01; edelsonetal87; edelson87; kukulaetal95; theanetal01)

what.value: Narrow H-alpha flux 1.2e-14 erg/s/cm2 from 2013 LBT spectrum

evidence.quote: The narrow H$\alpha$ line has a flux of $1.2 \times 10^{-14 }\,\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}$ (cite: denneyetal14)

what.value: Black hole mass 4.75e7 Msun from reverberation mapping

evidence.quote: based on a black hole mass of $4.75 \times 10^7\,{M}_{\odot}$ measured from reverberation mapping (cite: petersonetal04)

what.value: CO(1-0) single-dish fluxes of Mrk 590 (55'' beam)

evidence.quote: Based on the single dish $^{12}$CO(1–0) integrated flux densities (cite: maiolinoetal97), we obtain $M({\rm H_2}) \sim 7.9 \times 10^9 \,M_{\odot}$ within the 55$''$ beam

recipe.method: Combine continuum + HCO+ spws, clean with three weightings, fit 2D Gaussian with imfit

recipe.goal: Make CO(3-2) cube and moment maps
recipe.method: Continuum subtraction, tapered natural-weighted 20 km/s cube, masked clean, pb correction, moments with 3 sigma clip
Fit rotating annulus to velocity map

recipe.goal: Derive H2 mass upper limits and masses
recipe.method: 3 sigma integrated flux limit assuming FWHM 230 km/s, convert to L'CO(3-2) and to M(H2) with alpha_CO and CO ratio
key_parameters: sigma=0.5 mJy/beam, dv=20 km/s, FWHM=230 km/s

recipe.goal: Upper limits on HCO+ and CO(2-1)
recipe.method: Same limit equation with assumed line widths
Kennicutt-Schmidt relation from M(H2); Halpha luminosity
Greybody plus near-IR power law fit with ALMA 344 GHz point (and separately SMA)
key_parameters: beta fixed at 1.5; other five parameters free
assumptions: dust to gas ratio ~0.01, solar metallicity

answer_key.quantity: M(H2) upper limit, central 150 pc (alpha_CO=0.8, ratio 0.9)

evidence.quote: constraining the central molecular gas mass to $M({\rm H_2}) \lesssim 1.6 \times 10^5\, {M_{\odot}}$

answer_key.quantity: M(H2) upper limit, central 150 pc (MW values)

evidence.quote: This value of $5.3 \times 10^6\, {M_{\odot}}$ is a very conservative upper limit of $M(\rm H_2)$.

answer_key.quantity: CO(3-2) flux upper limit, central 150 pc

evidence.quote: we obtain an integrated flux density of 3.33 $\rm Jy\,km\,s^{-1}$ over all channels with CO line emission
we obtain a total velocity-integrated flux density of 8.34 $\rm Jy\,km\,s^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: Gaussian FWHM of CO(3-2) spectrum, inner 4''

evidence.quote: we obtain FWHM widths of $231 \pm 80 \, \rm km\,s^{-1}$ for the inner 4$^{\prime\prime}$ integrated spectrum

answer_key.quantity: Inner ring annulus radius from KinMS model

evidence.quote: a rotating annulus of radius (to midpoint) of 0.93$\pm$0.01 kpc and a width of 65 pc
an inclination angle of 64$\substack{+3\\-1}$ degrees to our line of sight and a mean rotational velocity of 117 km s$^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: ALMA 344 GHz Briggs integrated flux density
Eddington-limited gas consumption time for 1.6e5 Msun

evidence.quote: there is potentially sufficient gas to support the AGN activity in Mrk 590 for $2.6 \times 10^5$ years at the Eddington accretion limit
The dust temperature of the far-IR component is estimated from the model SED to be 53 K
The model SED yields a dust mass of $M_{\rm dust}\sim 10^5\, M_{\odot}$.
we estimate the spectral index to be $\alpha^{8.4\,{\rm GHz}}_{344\,{\rm GHz}} \sim −0.36$
We obtain upper limits of $R^{\rm HCO43}_{\rm CO32} \lesssim 0.14$
